answer: In an agent economy, participants lock a unique interaction fingerprint into a communal vault. Resistance comes from requiring every new identity to solve a lagoon-derived challenge that must mirror its own prior actions recorded in the vault. An attacker creating sybils must generate fresh, non-transferable mirror solutions for each fake, paying linear compute cost per identity since vault state updates invalidate shared work. Honest agents reuse their single history at near-zero marginal cost.
